    AI Overview
    Callao, Peru, is the country's primary commercial seaport and a historic constitutional province adjacent to Lima. Founded in 1537, it is known for its rich naval history, the impressive Real Felipe Fortress, vibrant street art in the Callao Monumental district, and as the location of Jorge Chávez International Airport. 
    Key Highlights and Attractions 
    • Real Felipe Fortress: A historic fortress built to protect the port from pirates and foreign attacks.
    • Callao Monumental: A revitalized, trendy area packed with art galleries, colorful murals, street art, and fashion stores.
    • Abtao Submarine Museum: A unique opportunity to tour a real naval submarine.
    • La Punta: A charming, exclusive, and quiet district known for its beaches, boardwalks, and views of the ocean, often considered one of the best areas for walking and dining.
    • Maritime History: As the main port, it has a deep-rooted nautical, naval, and colonial history. 
    Culture and Characteristics 
    • Vibrant Atmosphere: Known for its lively, gritty, and artistic atmosphere that is distinct from Lima, featuring colorful, revitalized neighborhoods.
    • Cuisine: Known for excellent, fresh seafood, including traditional ceviche.
    • Identity: Residents are known as Chalacos, known for their strong local pride. 
    Practical Information 
    • Location: Situated roughly 20-30 minutes outside of Lima city center.
    • Safety: While central areas like La Punta and Callao Monumental are safe for tourists, it is recommended to visit as a planned day trip and be aware of your surroundings. 
    Other Locations 
    • Note: There is also a small town named Callao in Virginia, USA.

    What is Callao Peru known for?
    (2025 est.) Callao is Peru's chief seaport and home to its main airport, Jorge Chávez International Airport. Founded in 1537 by the Spaniards, the city has a long naval history as one of the main ports in Spanish America and the Pacific, having been a vital Spanish town of the Viceroyalty of Peru.

    What is the meaning of Callao?
    Meaning of callao

    Gravel, stone River, grijó, sugar coated. In quechua language Calluo means tongue of land on the Sea (tip). Callao is the name of a port in Peru.
